To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) preference information is critical for the identification and estimation of Bayesian learning, (2) Bayesian learning is not a general phenomenon, but rather one that is specific to a particular product category, and (3) the Bayesian learning process is not as strong as previously believed.

(1) preference heterogeneity and learning can be separated, (2) the inclusion of measured preference information reduces the need for state dependence and learning at both the aggregate and individual levels, (3) the inclusion of preference heterogeneity reduces the need for Bayesian updating, and (4) the inclusion of both measured preferences and heterogeneity results in an almost complete elimination of the learning process.

(a) preference heterogeneity is an important source of state dependence, and (b) in the absence of preference heterogeneity, the learning behavior is vastly overstated and, in particular, the aggregate learning is overestimated and the individual learning is underestimated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of preference parameters in Bayesian learning models and shows that the failure to account for preference heterogeneities leads to overestimated state-dependent behavior.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Bayesian learning is an interesting and useful framework for modeling state dependence but that the presence of preference heterogeneity must be adequately accounted for in any attempt to estimate learning parameters.
the inclusion of preference information is essential for understanding the role of state dependence and that Bayesian learning is not as pervasive as has been suggested in previous work.
preference heterogeneity can be a significant source of state dependence, and that Bayesian learning models should be interpreted with caution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the failure to adequately disentangle preference heterogeneity from state dependence may result in over- or underestimation of learning behavior.
the inclusion of preference information is critical in any Bayesian learning model.
preference heterogeneity can have a large impact on the measurement of state dependence and, as such, it is important to account for this heterogeneity when estimating Bayesian learning models.
